statement: Barnette’s conjecture · 1969. Every cubic, bipartite, 3-connected planar graph is Hamiltonian.
title: Barnette’s conjecture

statement: Every n-vertex tree has a bijective vertex labeling by 0,…,n−1 whose n−1 absolute edge differences are pairwise distinct.
title: Graceful Tree conjecture

statement: Vertex Reconstruction conjecture · 1941, attributed to Ulam, with Kelly’s 1942 formulation. Graphs on at least three vertices are determined by their vertex-deleted decks.
title: Vertex Reconstruction conjecture

statement: Edge Reconstruction conjecture · 1964, due to Harary. A graph with at least four edges is determined by its edge-deleted deck.
title: Edge Reconstruction conjecture

statement: Hoffmann-Ostenhof’s 3-Decomposition conjecture · 2011. Every connected cubic graph has an edge partition into a spanning tree, a 2-regular subgraph, and a matching.
title: Hoffmann-Ostenhof’s 3-Decomposition conjecture

statement: Sheehan’s conjecture · 1975. No 4-regular graph has exactly one Hamiltonian cycle.
title: Sheehan’s conjecture

statement: Kotzig’s \(P_k\)-graph conjecture · 1974. For every \(k\ge3\), no finite graph has exactly one simple length-\(k\) path between each pair of distinct vertices.
title: Kotzig’s \(P_k\)-graph conjecture

statement: Jaeger’s Petersen Coloring conjecture · 1988. Every bridgeless cubic graph has a Petersen coloring, equivalently a compatible local edge map to the Petersen graph.
title: Jaeger’s Petersen Coloring conjecture

statement: Berge–Fulkerson conjecture · 1971–1972. Every bridgeless cubic graph has six perfect matchings covering every edge exactly twice.
title: Berge–Fulkerson conjecture

statement: Fan–Raspaud conjecture · 1994. Every bridgeless cubic graph has three perfect matchings with empty common intersection.
title: Fan–Raspaud conjecture

statement: Tutte’s 5-Flow conjecture · 1954. Every bridgeless graph admits a nowhere-zero 5-flow.
title: Tutte’s 5-Flow conjecture

statement: Tutte’s 3-Flow conjecture · 1972. Every 4-edge-connected graph has a nowhere-zero 3-flow.
title: Tutte’s 3-Flow conjecture

statement: Bouchet’s 6-Flow conjecture · 1983. Every flow-admissible signed graph has a nowhere-zero integer 6-flow.
title: Bouchet’s 6-Flow conjecture

statement: Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture · 1978. The first open case asks whether every oriented n-vertex graph of minimum outdegree at least n/3 contains a directed triangle.
title: Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture

statement: Every finite loopless simple digraph of minimum outdegree at least seven contains four vertex-disjoint directed cycles; antiparallel arcs and directed 2-cycles are allowed.
title: Bermond–Thomassen conjecture

statement: Prime-power conjecture for finite projective planes · explicitly posed in 1981 by Erdős, with older folklore antecedents. Every finite projective plane has prime-power order.
title: Prime-power conjecture for finite projective planes

statement: Seymour’s Second Neighborhood conjecture · 1990. Every oriented graph has a vertex whose second out-neighborhood is at least as large as its first.
title: Seymour’s Second Neighborhood conjecture

statement: Conway’s Thrackle conjecture · late 1960s, commonly dated 1969. A planar thrackle drawing has no more edges than vertices.
title: Conway’s Thrackle conjecture

statement: For every n, the crossing number of K_n equals floor(n/2)·floor((n−1)/2)·floor((n−2)/2)·floor((n−3)/2)/4.
title: Harary–Hill conjecture

statement: For all m,n, the crossing number of K_(m,n) equals floor(m/2)·floor((m−1)/2)·floor(n/2)·floor((n−1)/2).
title: Zarankiewicz’s complete-bipartite crossing conjecture

statement: Albertson’s conjecture · 2007. Every graph with chromatic number r has crossing number at least that of K_r.
title: Albertson’s conjecture

statement: Hadwiger’s conjecture · 1943. Every graph with chromatic number at least t contains K_t as a minor.
title: Hadwiger’s conjecture

statement: Total Coloring conjecture · Behzad 1965 and Vizing 1968. Every graph has a total coloring using at most Δ+2 colors.
title: Total Coloring conjecture

statement: List Edge Coloring conjecture · Vizing 1975 and Erdős–Rubin–Taylor 1979. Every graph’s list chromatic index equals its ordinary chromatic index.
title: List Edge Coloring conjecture

statement: Acyclic Edge Coloring conjecture · Fiamčík 1978, sharpened by Alon–Sudakov–Zaks in 2001. Every graph has an acyclic edge coloring with at most Δ+2 colors.
title: Acyclic Edge Coloring conjecture

statement: Erdős–Nešetřil Strong Chromatic Index conjecture · 1985. For even Δ, every graph has a strong edge coloring with at most 5Δ²/4 colors.
title: Erdős–Nešetřil Strong Chromatic Index conjecture

statement: Wegner’s planar graph-square conjecture · 1977. Its Δ=4 case predicts that the square of every planar graph is 9-colorable.
title: Wegner’s planar graph-square conjecture

statement: Borodin–Kostochka conjecture · 1977. Every graph of maximum degree Δ at least nine satisfies χ ≤ max(Δ − 1, ω).
title: Borodin–Kostochka conjecture

statement: Linear Arboricity conjecture · Akiyama, Exoo, and Harary, 1980. A graph’s edges can be partitioned into at most ceil((Δ+1)/2) linear forests.
title: Linear Arboricity conjecture

statement: Every even integer N≥4 is the sum of two primes.
title: Goldbach

statement: The Collatz map T(n)=n/2 for even n and T(n)=3n+1 for odd n has no positive-integer cycle other than 1→4→2→1.
title: Collatz, finite-cycle route

statement: For every integer n≥1, there is a prime strictly between n² and (n+1)².
title: Legendre prime-between-squares

statement: For every integer n≥2, there are positive integers x,y,z such that 4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z.
title: Erdős–Straus

statement: If φ(n) divides n−1, then n is prime.
title: Lehmer totient

statement: There are no positive integers a,b,c,u,v,w,d satisfying a²+b²=u², a²+c²=v², b²+c²=w², and a²+b²+c²=d².
title: No perfect cuboid

statement: For integers x>y>1 and m,n>2, the equation (x^m−1)/(x−1)=(y^n−1)/(y−1) has only the solutions (x,y,m,n)=(5,2,3,5) and (90,2,3,13).
title: Goormaghtigh

statement: The only positive integer solutions of n!+1=m² have n∈{4,5,7}.
title: Brocard–Ramanujan

statement: Every circulant Hadamard matrix has order 1 or 4.
title: Circulant Hadamard nonexistence

statement: Every Barker sequence has length at most 13.
title: No long Barker sequence

statement: If sum(a_i^k, i=1,…,m)=sum(b_j^k, j=1,…,n) for positive integers with a_i≠b_j for every i,j, then m+n≥k.
title: Lander–Parkin–Selfridge

statement: For every positive even n, the numbers of even and odd Latin squares of order n are different.
title: Alon–Tarsi Latin-square parity

statement: For all positive integers a≤b, the symmetric function h_b[h_a]−h_a[h_b] is Schur-positive.
title: Foulkes plethysm

statement: For every k, the tensor square of the irreducible symmetric-group representation indexed by the staircase partition ρ_k=(k,k−1,…,1) contains every irreducible representation of S_(k(k+1)/2).
title: Saxl staircase square

statement: No two nonisomorphic trees have the same chromatic symmetric function.
title: Stanley tree chromatic symmetric function

statement: Every origin-symmetric convex body K in R^d satisfies vol(K)·vol(K°)≥4^d/d!.
title: Symmetric Mahler volume product

statement: Every centrally symmetric d-polytope has at least 3^d nonempty faces.
title: Kalai \(3^d\)-faces

statement: Every convex body in R³ can be illuminated by at most eight directions.
title: Hadwiger–Levi illumination

statement: Every bounded subset of R⁴ can be partitioned into five subsets, each of strictly smaller diameter.
title: Borsuk in dimension four

statement: Every synchronizing deterministic finite automaton with n states has a reset word of length at most (n−1)².
title: Černý–Starke synchronizing-word conjecture

statement: Every nontrivial monotone isomorphism-invariant property of n-vertex graphs is evasive: some input forces every deterministic decision tree to query all binomial(n,2) possible edges.
title: Aanderaa–Karp–Rosenberg evasiveness conjecture

statement: Conforti–Cornuéjols replication conjecture · 1993. It says every clutter with the packing property has the max-flow min-cut property (attribution and status).
title: Conforti–Cornuéjols replication conjecture

statement: Every r-uniform r-partite hypergraph satisfies τ≤(r−1)ν, where τ is its transversal number and ν its matching number.
title: Ryser’s \(r\)-partite hypergraph conjecture

statement: Every instance of four agents with nonnegative additive valuations admits a complete EFX allocation: for every pair of agents i,j and every good g in j's bundle with positive value to i, v_i(A_i)≥v_i(A_j\{g}).
title: Complete EFX for additive goods

statement: Circuit-Hirsch conjecture · 2015. The circuit analogue predicts diameter at most \(f-d\) for a \(d\)-polyhedron with \(f\) facets; the 2016 preprint cites the original BFH15 formulation (source).
title: Circuit-Hirsch conjecture

statement: Dittert’s permanent conjecture · by 1983. For a nonnegative \(n\times n\) matrix \(A\) of total sum \(n\), let \(r_i,c_j\) be its row and column sums and \(\phi(A)=\prod_i r_i+\prod_j c_j-\operatorname{per}(A)\). Dittert conjectured \(\phi(A)\le2-n!/n^n\); Minc attributed the problem to Eric Dittert (current attribution).
title: Dittert’s permanent conjecture

statement: In every finite digraph, the maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint dijoins equals the minimum size of a nonempty dicut. A dicut is δ⁺(U) for a nonempty proper vertex set U with δ⁻(U)=∅, and a dijoin is an arc set meeting every dicut.
title: Woodall’s dijoin-packing conjecture

statement: Samuels’s small-deviation conjecture · 1966. For \(0\le\mu_1\le\cdots\le\mu_n\) with \(\sum_i\mu_i<1\), it predicts that over independent nonnegative \(X_i\) with \(E X_i=\mu_i\), \(\inf P(\sum_iX_i<1)=\min_{0\le t<n}\prod_{i=t+1}^n\left(1-\frac{\mu_i}{1-\sum_{j=1}^t\mu_j}\right)\) (original).
title: Samuels’s small-deviation conjecture

statement: Gaussian product inequality · 2012 general form. For a centered Gaussian vector and nonnegative exponents, Li and Wei conjectured \(E\prod_j\lvert X_j\rvert^{\alpha_j}\ge\prod_jE\lvert X_j\rvert^{\alpha_j}\), extending Frenkel’s 2008 result (history).
title: Gaussian product inequality

statement: For every complex square matrix A and polynomial p, ||p(A)||₂≤2·max{|p(z)|: z is in the numerical range W(A)}.
title: Crouzeix’s conjecture

statement: The normalized Atiyah–Sutcliffe determinant of every configuration of distinct points in R³ is nonzero.
title: Atiyah–Sutcliffe determinant conjecture

statement: Every convex polyhedron has a nonoverlapping planar unfolding obtained by cutting a spanning tree of its edges.
title: Dürer–Shephard edge-unfolding conjecture

statement: Sidorenko’s graph-homomorphism conjecture · 1991. Sidorenko conjectured that every finite bipartite \(H\) and graphon \(W\) satisfy \(t_H(W)\ge t_{K_2}(W)^{e(H)}\) (original publication).
title: Sidorenko’s graph-homomorphism conjecture

statement: In R³, moving the centers of congruent balls so that no pairwise distance increases cannot increase the volume of their union.
title: Kneser–Poulsen contraction conjecture

statement: A strongly regular graph with parameters (99,14,1,2) exists.
title: Conway’s 99-graph problem

statement: Smale’s mean-value conjecture · 1981. For a degree-\(d\) polynomial \(P\) and \(z\) with \(P'(z)\ne0\), Smale conjectured \(\min_{P'(\zeta)=0}\left\lvert\frac{P(z)-P(\zeta)}{(z-\zeta)P'(z)}\right\rvert\le(d-1)/d\) (original).
title: Smale’s mean-value conjecture

statement: Chollet’s permanent conjecture · 1982. Chollet proposed \(\operatorname{per}(A\circ B)\le\operatorname{per}(A)\operatorname{per}(B)\) for Hermitian PSD matrices (history).
title: Chollet’s permanent conjecture

statement: Log-Brunn–Minkowski conjecture · 2012. For origin-symmetric convex bodies \(K,L\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(0\le\lambda\le1\), it asserts \(V((1-\lambda)\cdot K+_0\lambda\cdot L)\ge V(K)^{1-\lambda}V(L)^\lambda\), where the log-sum is the Wulff body with support datum \(h_K^{1-\lambda}h_L^\lambda\) (original).
title: Log-Brunn–Minkowski conjecture

statement: For every 1<p<∞, the L^p operator norm of the Beurling–Ahlfors transform equals p*−1, where p*=max(p,p/(p−1)).
title: Beurling–Ahlfors norm conjecture

statement: For every permutation σ of the vertices of the d-dimensional hypercube, the doubly directed hypercube has pairwise edge-disjoint paths from each v to σ(v), where opposite uses of an edge are allowed.
title: Szymanski’s hypercube-routing conjecture

statement: Exact Beck–Fiala \(t\)-bound · 1981. Beck and Fiala conjectured discrepancy at most \(t\) when every element occurs in at most \(t\) sets (historical form).
title: Exact Beck–Fiala \(t\)-bound

statement: Hadwiger–Nelson exact-value hypothesis \(\chi(\mathbb R^2)=5\) · April 2018. This post-de Grey hypothesis has no canonical proposer; his construction made 5 the lower endpoint (paper).
title: Hadwiger–Nelson exact-value hypothesis \(\chi(\mathbb R^2)=5\)

statement: Perfect one-factorisation conjecture · Anton Kotzig, 1963. Every complete graph \(K_n\) of even order \(n\ge4\) has an edge partition into perfect matchings such that every pair of matchings forms a Hamilton cycle (current formulation and history).
title: Perfect one-factorisation conjecture

statement: Cabling conjecture · 1983. González-Acuña and Short proposed that reducible surgery on a nontrivial knot must be cabling surgery on a cable knot (history).
title: Cabling conjecture

statement: No nontrivial knot in S³ has orientation-preservingly homeomorphic Dehn fillings along two distinct slopes.
title: Purely cosmetic surgery conjecture

statement: Every crossing change that preserves a knot's isotopy type is nugatory.
title: Cosmetic crossing conjecture

statement: In every finite dimension d≥2 there exists a Weyl–Heisenberg-covariant symmetric informationally complete POVM.
title: Zauner’s Weyl–Heisenberg SIC existence conjecture

statement: Zauner’s dimension-six MUB conjecture · 1999. Zauner conjectured that at most three mutually unbiased bases exist in \(\mathbb C^6\) (author’s history).
title: Zauner’s dimension-six MUB conjecture

statement: The composition of any two finite-dimensional PPT quantum channels is entanglement breaking.
title: PPT-squared conjecture

statement: Every centrally symmetric convex body X in R^(2n) satisfies c_EHZ(X)^n≤n!·vol(X).
title: Centrally symmetric Viterbo conjecture

statement: For every graph G other than a cycle C_(4k+1), the sum over Laplacian eigenvalues μᵢ≥2 of (μᵢ−2)² is at most (1−1/d₁) times the sum of dᵢ(dᵢ−1).
title: Li–Guo Laplacian degree-sequence inequality

statement: If every edge of a graph joins vertices of different degrees, then the multiset of absolute endpoint-degree differences is graphical.
title: Positive-edge graph imbalance conjecture

statement: Every connected n-vertex graph with at least n+1 edges has s⁺(G)≥n, where s⁺ is the sum of squares of the positive adjacency eigenvalues.
title: Positive square-energy strengthening

statement: For every n-vertex graph and k≤3n/4, the k-th Laplacian eigenvalues of G and its complement satisfy μₖ(G)μₖ(complement(G))≤n(n−k).
title: Nordhaus–Gaddum product for the \(k\)-th Laplacian eigenvalue

statement: For reversible second-order cellular automaton rule 115, the configuration family 1(01)^k has period P(2i)=(2·4^(2i+2)−7·4^(i+1)+5)/3 for every natural number i.
title: Rule 115 even-period formula

statement: The largest fifth pivot growth factor under Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting is the unique real root in [4,5] of the explicit degree-61 polynomial P₅ in Equation (2.15) of the source.
title: Largest fifth pivot under Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting

statement: Every loopless bridgeless graph satisfies T_G(1,1)≤max(T_G(2,0),T_G(0,2)).
title: Graphical Merino–Welsh conjecture

statement: The maximum number of edges in a C₄-free subgraph of the eight-dimensional cube Q₈ is 680.
title: \(\operatorname{ex}(Q_8,C_4)=680\)

statement: For all nonnegative k and ℓ, the integer complexity of 2^k3^ℓ equals 2k+3ℓ.
title: Integer complexity of \(2^k3^\ell\)

statement: The Erdős–Szekeres number ES(7) equals 33.
title: Erdős–Szekeres exact-value conjecture

statement: The diagonal Ramsey number R(5,5) equals 43.
title: \(R(5,5)=43\)

statement: If the ground set of a rank-n matroid is partitioned into n bases, those elements can be rearranged into n disjoint transversal bases.
title: Rota’s basis conjecture

statement: Every Latin square of odd order has a transversal.
title: Ryser’s odd-order Latin-square transversal conjecture

statement: Every numerical semigroup with conductor c, embedding dimension e, and L the semigroup elements below c satisfies e|L|≥c.
title: Wilf’s numerical-semigroup conjecture

statement: The integrality gap of the subtour-elimination linear program for metric TSP is at most 4/3.
title: Metric-TSP \(4/3\) subtour-LP integrality-gap conjecture

statement: Every triangle-free graph on 5n vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most n² edges.
title: Erdős problem #23: triangle-free bipartization

statement: Every convex polygon has a vertex with no four other vertices equidistant from it.
title: Erdős problem #97: equal distances in a convex polygon

statement: If f(n) is the maximum sum of side lengths of n squares with pairwise disjoint interiors inside the unit square, then f(k²+1)=k.
title: Erdős problem #106: square-packing side-length sum

statement: Among monic complex polynomials of degree n, the length of the lemniscate |p(z)|=1 is maximized by p(z)=zⁿ−1.
title: Erdős problem #114: polynomial lemniscate length

statement: If every induced subgraph on at least floor(n/2) vertices has more than n²/50 edges, then the graph contains a triangle.
title: Erdős problem #128: half-density triangle condition

statement: For distinct integers 1<n₁<⋯<nₖ with reciprocal sum one, some consecutive denominator gap is at least three.
title: Erdős problem #287: unit-fraction denominator gaps

statement: For every k≥1, lcm(1,…,pₖ₊₁−1) < pₖ lcm(1,…,pₖ).
title: Erdős problem #458: primorial LCM inequality

statement: For a finite set A and its multiples B, every m>n≥max(A) satisfies |B∩[1,m]|/m < 2|B∩[1,n]|/n.
title: Erdős problem #488: divisibility-set density

statement: Every n-vertex graph with at least ((k−1)/2)n+1 edges contains every tree on k+1 vertices.
title: Erdős problem #548: dense-graph tree embedding

statement: Every connected n-vertex graph can be partitioned into at most ceil(n/2) edge-disjoint paths.
title: Erdős problem #583: Gallai path decomposition

statement: If a Kₖ-free graph has chromatic number k and a,b≥2 with a+b=k+1, then it has two disjoint subgraphs of chromatic numbers at least a and b.
title: Erdős problem #628: chromatic splitting

statement: For every 1≤i<j≤n/2, some prime p≥i divides gcd(binomial(n,i),binomial(n,j)).
title: Erdős problem #699: prime divisors of binomial gcds

statement: For any trees T₂,…,Tₙ with Tₖ having k vertices, Kₙ is their edge-disjoint union.
title: Erdős problem #743: tree packing into a complete graph

statement: The sequence counting independent sets by size is unimodal for every tree or forest.
title: Erdős problem #993: unimodality of tree independent sets

statement: Every n-point planar set with no three collinear determines at least floor(n/2) distances, and some point sees that many distinct distances.
title: Erdős problem #1082: distinct distances in general position

statement: No finite distinct covering system has all moduli odd.
title: Erdős problem #7: odd distinct covering systems

statement: If a graph is an edge-disjoint union of n copies of Kₙ, then its chromatic number is n.
title: Erdős problem #19: chromatic number of clique unions

statement: There do not exist finite prime sets P,Q for which the product of their reciprocal sums equals one.
title: Erdős problem #307: a product of reciprocal-prime sums

statement: There is no 2-full integer n for which n+1 is 3-full.
title: Erdős problem #366: consecutive 2-full and 3-full numbers

statement: Every finite nonzero subset of a prime field has an ordering with all partial sums distinct.
title: Erdős problem #475: distinct partial sums in finite fields

statement: Every n-vertex tree T has two-colour Ramsey number at most 2n−2.
title: Erdős problem #547: a Ramsey bound for trees

statement: For k≥n≥3, except n=k=3, R(Cₖ,Kₙ)=(k−1)(n−1)+1.
title: Erdős problem #551: cycle-versus-clique Ramsey number

statement: For every n≥4, the three-colour Ramsey number of Cₙ is at most 4n−3.
title: Erdős problem #556: three-colour cycle Ramsey bound

statement: If at least n/2 vertices of an n-vertex graph have degree at least n/2, then the graph contains every tree on at most n/2 vertices.
title: Erdős problem #580: half-dense tree containment

statement: For every n>24, max over m<n of m+τ(m) is greater than n+2.
title: Erdős problem #647: divisor-count record inequality

statement: The product of a coprime arithmetic progression of length at least four is never a perfect power.
title: Erdős problem #672: perfect-power progression products

statement: Every n-vertex diameter-two graph in which deleting any edge increases the diameter has at most n²/4 edges.
title: Erdős problem #742: diameter-two edge-critical graphs

statement: No k>2 admits a (k+1)-colouring of the k-subsets of [2k] in which every (k+1)-set sees all colours.
title: Erdős problem #835: local-rainbow hypergraph colouring

statement: The largest A⊆[N] for which ab+1 is never squarefree is always achieved by the numbers congruent to 7 modulo 25.
title: Erdős problem #848: squarefree-product-avoiding sets

statement: Every simple graph of maximum degree at most six has a crossing-free three-dimensional orthogonal grid drawing with at most two bends per edge.
title: Two-bend 3D orthogonal graph drawings

statement: Every simply connected polyhedron with an even quadrilateral surface mesh has a compatible interior hexahedral mesh whose cells have planar faces.
title: Hexahedral meshing

statement: The bistellar flip graph of every general-position point set in R³ is connected.
title: Flip-graph connectivity in three dimensions

statement: Every convex three-dimensional polytope has a tetrahedralization whose dual graph has a Hamiltonian path.
title: Hamiltonian tetrahedralizations

statement: No finite collection of pairwise disjoint two-sided segment mirrors traps every ray from one disjoint point source.
title: Trapping light with segment mirrors

statement: Any two general-position planar n-point sets with equal convex-hull size have combinatorially compatible triangulations.
title: Compatible triangulations

statement: Every closed polyhedron with simply connected facets has a nonoverlapping one-piece vertex unfolding.
title: Vertex-unfolding polyhedra

statement: Every closed polyhedron can be cut along its surface and unfolded into one nonoverlapping planar piece.
title: General unfoldings of nonconvex polyhedra

statement: The arrangement graph of any set of great circles with no triple intersection is vertex three-colourable.
title: Three-colouring great-circle arrangements

statement: Every genus-zero polycube has a nonoverlapping edge unfolding when all surface cube edges may be cut.
title: Edge-unfolding genus-zero polycubes

statement: Every immersed spherical polyhedral surface made from equal regular pentagons bounds a union of face-glued solid dodecahedra.
title: Polyhedral surfaces with regular pentagon faces

statement: Every convex polyhedron has a nonoverlapping zipper unfolding cut along one vertex-spanning path.
title: Zipper unfoldings of convex polyhedra

statement: Every finite connected simple graph other than K₂ has a bijective edge labeling by 1,…,m with pairwise distinct incident-label sums at its vertices.
title: Antimagic labeling conjecture

statement: A connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane.
title: Negami planar-cover conjecture

statement: Any two tuples of matroid bases with the same multiset union are connected by symmetric exchanges.
title: White symmetric-exchange conjecture

statement: For all finite connected graphs G,H, the pebbling number of G□H is at most the product of the pebbling numbers of G and H.
title: Graham graph-pebbling product conjecture

statement: Every family of n matchings of size n+1 in a bipartite multigraph has a rainbow matching of size n.
title: Aharoni–Berger rainbow-matching conjecture

statement: Every finite connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamiltonian path.
title: Lovász vertex-transitive Hamilton-path conjecture

statement: The D₅ root-lattice density is optimal among unit-sphere packings in Euclidean dimension five.
title: D₅ sphere-packing optimality conjecture

statement: The E₆ root-lattice density is optimal among unit-sphere packings in Euclidean dimension six.
title: E₆ sphere-packing optimality conjecture

statement: Every finite graph with minimum degree at least three contains a cycle of length 2^k for some integer k≥2.
title: Erdős problem #64: power-of-two cycle

statement: If a finite graph has at most k pairwise edge-disjoint triangles, then deleting at most 2k edges can make it triangle-free.
title: Erdős problem #167: triangle packing versus cover

statement: Every integer n>1 can be written as n=x+y with positive integers x,y such that 2^x+y is prime.
title: OEIS A231201 power-of-two prime-sum conjecture

statement: Every integer n>1 can be written as n=x+y with positive integers x,y such that x+ny and x²+ny² are both prime.
title: OEIS A232174 two-prime representation conjecture

statement: Every nonnegative integer n can be written as n=x²+y²+z²+w² for nonnegative integers x,y,z,w such that x⁴+1680y³z is a square.
title: Sun's 1680 four-square conjecture

statement: Every nonnegative integer n can be written as n=x²+y²+z²+w² for nonnegative integers with z≤w, where x and x+24y are both squares.
title: OEIS A281976 restricted four-square conjecture

statement: Every integer n>1 can be written as n=a²+b²+3^c+5^d for nonnegative integers a,b,c,d.
title: OEIS A303656 squares-and-powers conjecture

statement: Every positive integer n can be written as C(w+2,2)+C(x+3,4)+C(y+5,6)+C(z+7,8) for nonnegative integers w,x,y,z.
title: Sun's 2-4-6-8 conjecture

statement: Every integer n>1 can be written as n=(2^a3^b)²+(2^c5^d)²+x²+y² for nonnegative integers a,b,c,d,x,y.
title: OEIS A308734 restricted power-square conjecture

statement: For every prime p, there is an integer k such that k²+1
title: Sun's square-plus-one primitive-root conjecture

statement: Every composite n satisfying φ(n+12)=φ(n)+12 and σ(n+12)=σ(n)+12 has the form n=p(p+8), where p,p+2,p+6,p+8 are all prime.
title: A056777 prime-quadruple characterization conjecture

statement: Every positive integer n satisfying σ(n)=2·usigma(n), where usigma is the sum of unitary divisors, is congruent to 108 modulo 216.
title: A063880 residue-108 conjecture

statement: The only n satisfying σ(n)=2·usigma(n) with no proper divisor satisfying the same identity is n=108.
title: A063880 unique primitive-term conjecture

statement: If φ(k²+1)=k·φ(k+1) and k≠8, then k+1 is prime.
title: A067720 unique composite-successor conjecture

statement: There is no positive integer n such that σ(σ(n))=5n, where σ is the sum of positive divisors.
title: No positive (2,5)-perfect number

statement: Every polynomial map F:ℂ²→ℂ² whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero constant is a polynomial automorphism.
title: Plane Jacobian conjecture: rational-collision variant

statement: For every finite simple connected graph G, the largest number of vertices in an induced tree is at least floor(girth(G)/2)−1+max_v α(G[N(v)]), where the girth is 0 for an acyclic graph.
title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 141

statement: For every nontrivial finite connected simple graph G, the largest order b(G) of an induced bipartite subgraph is at least floor(ecc_avg(G)+max_v α(G[N(v)])).
title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 19

statement: Every nontrivial finite connected simple graph G satisfying tree(G)=ceil(1+l_avg(G)), where tree(G) is the largest induced-tree order and l_avg(G) is the average neighborhood independence number, has a Hamiltonian path.
title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 200

statement: For every nontrivial finite connected simple graph G, the largest induced-forest order f(G) is at least ceil((p(G)+b(G)+1)/2), where p(G) is the minimum number of vertex-disjoint paths covering V(G) and b(G) is the largest induced-bipartite order.
title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 40

statement: Every finite loopless sink-free digraph D has an independent vertex set Q of size at most |V(D)|/2 such that every vertex of D can reach Q by a directed path of length at most two.
title: Small quasi-kernel conjecture

statement: For every finite simple graph G and every integer k greater than its maximum degree, every assignment of a k-element color list to each vertex has a proper list coloring in which no color is used more than ceil(|V(G)|/k) times.
title: Equitable list-coloring conjecture

statement: For every complex polynomial P of degree at least two and every complex z, some critical point c of P satisfies |P(z)-P(c)|≤|P′(z)|·|z-c|.
title: Smale’s constant-one mean-value problem

statement: For every prime p, the Mersenne number 2^p−1 is square-free.
title: Prime-exponent Mersenne square-freeness conjecture

statement: If a terminal set T in a finite graph is 2k-edge-connected, then the graph contains k pairwise edge-disjoint Steiner trees spanning T.
title: Kriesell’s Steiner-tree packing conjecture

statement: If the ground set of a finite matroid can be partitioned into k disjoint bases, then its elements have a cyclic ordering in which every rank-many consecutive elements form a basis.
title: Cyclic ordering conjecture for matroids

statement: For any two bases A and B of a matroid and every subset X of A, there is an equally sized subset Y of B and orderings of X and Y such that, after every paired prefix exchange, both resulting sets are bases.
title: Kotlar–Ziv serial symmetric exchange conjecture

statement: Let b be the maximum, over the vertices of a rationally edge-weighted bipartite multigraph, of the minimum number of unit bins needed for the incident edge weights. The edges have a coloring with at most 2b−1 colors such that, at every vertex, the total incident weight of each color is at most one.
title: Chung–Ross weighted bipartite edge-coloring conjecture

statement: Let M be a loopless rank-k matroid whose ground set is the disjoint union of k bases. Every partition of that ground set into k sets of size k has k−1 pairwise disjoint transversals that are bases of M.
title: Scrambled Rota conjecture

statement: If the common independent sets of two matroids on the same finite ground set admit a proper coloring with k colors, then they admit a proper coloring from every assignment of a size-k color list to each element.
title: List-coloring conjecture for two matroids

statement: For a loopless matroid M let Δ(M)=max over nonempty X of |X|/r_M(X). The common ground set of any two loopless matroids M₁ and M₂ can be partitioned into at most ceil(max(Δ(M₁),Δ(M₂)))+1 sets that are independent in both matroids.
title: Aharoni–Berger common-independent-set covering conjecture

statement: Let G=(V,E) be a finite graph of maximum degree Δ≥2, and let M be a matroid on V containing 2Δ pairwise disjoint bases. Then M contains 2Δ pairwise disjoint bases, each of which is a stable set of G.
title: Strong coloring conjecture for matroid–graph pairs

statement: Let D be a finite loopless digraph and k a positive integer. Define the k-norm of a path partition Π by |Π|ₖ=Σ_{P∈Π} min(|V(P)|,k). Every path partition of minimum k-norm has an orthogonal partial k-coloring: k pairwise disjoint stable sets of the underlying graph such that each P∈Π meets min(|V(P)|,k) distinct color classes.
title: Berge’s strong path-partition conjecture

statement: Let M₁,…,Mₖ be matroids with rank functions r₁,…,rₖ on the same finite ground set S, and let ℓ be a positive integer. If Σᵢ rᵢ(Xᵢ)≥(k−1)ℓ for every ordered partition S=X₁⊔⋯⊔Xₖ, then the matroids have a common independent set of cardinality ℓ.
title: Aharoni–Berger rank-partition conjecture

statement: For every positive integer k, every finite k-vertex-connected graph G, and every prescribed root r, there are k spanning trees T₁,…,Tₖ such that, for every vertex v≠r, the unique r–v paths in the trees are pairwise internally vertex-disjoint.
title: Zehavi–Itai independent spanning-trees conjecture

statement: Every finite connected graph G of genus g=|E(G)|−|V(G)|+1 has divisorial gonality gon(G)≤⌊(g+3)/2⌋; equivalently, G has an integer divisor of degree at most ⌊(g+3)/2⌋ and rank at least one.
title: Baker’s graph-gonality conjecture

statement: Let G=(V,E) be a finite bipartite graph, and let c₁,…,cₖ be positive real numbers with sum one. Then E can be partitioned into E₁,…,Eₖ so that, for every vertex v and every i, ⌊cᵢd_E(v)⌋≤d_{Eᵢ}(v)≤⌈cᵢd_E(v)⌉.
title: Correa–Goemans bipartite proportional-factors question

statement: For every positive integer k, every finite k-edge-connected graph G, and every prescribed root r, there are k spanning trees T₁,…,Tₖ such that, for every vertex v≠r, the unique r–v paths in the trees are pairwise edge-disjoint.
title: Zehavi–Itai edge-independent spanning-trees conjecture

statement: Let G be a finite undirected graph with a designated terminal set T. If T is 2k-element-connected in G—every two terminals have 2k paths that are pairwise disjoint in edges and nonterminal internal vertices—then G has an orientation in which T is k-element-connected in both directions.
title: Highly element-connected orientation conjecture

statement: Let B be a k-element subset of the cyclic group Z_n. Then there is a rank-k binary matroid on Z_n in which every cyclic translate B+i is a basis.
title: Binary matroid representation of cyclic families

statement: If every vertex of a finite-dimensional base polyhedron B lies in {-1,0,1}^n and the origin belongs to B, then B has a vertex v for which -v is also a vertex.
title: Opposite vertices of base polyhedra

statement: Let D=(V,A) be a finite digraph rooted at r, let k,l be positive integers, and let each arc have a positive integer capacity at most l. If the capacities admit a packing of kl spanning out-arborescences rooted at r, then they admit a packing of l k-arborescences, where each k-arborescence is the arc-disjoint union of k rooted spanning arborescences.
title: Capacitated packing of 2-arborescences

statement: Every smooth lattice polytope P has the integer decomposition property: for every positive integer k and every lattice point z in kP, there are lattice points z_1,...,z_k in P whose sum is z.
title: Oda's smooth-polytope integer-decomposition conjecture

statement: Every finite 3-arc-connected digraph D and every root r in V(D) have an arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescence and spanning in-arborescence, both rooted at r.
title: Disjoint in- and out-arborescences at arc-connectivity three

statement: Let D=(V,A) be an acyclic digraph, let r_1,...,r_k be designated roots, and let U_1,...,U_k be convex vertex sets with r_i in U_i. If, for every v, the paths r_i-to-v for all i with v in U_i can be chosen pairwise openly node-disjoint, then there are independent r_i-arborescences F_i with V(F_i)=U_i.
title: Independent arborescences on convex sets in acyclic digraphs

statement: Let G=(V,E) be an undirected graph with root r. If G is 4-edge-connected and G-v is 2-edge-connected for every v other than r, then G contains two edge-disjoint spanning subgraphs in each of which every vertex has two internally vertex-disjoint paths from r.
title: Rooted (2,2)-connected graph decomposition

statement: Every plane graph whose shortest facial boundary has length five has a not-necessarily-proper vertex 3-coloring in which all three colors occur on the boundary of every face.
title: Polychromatic plane-graph coloring at face size five
